title: Machine learning on plasma mtDNA fragmentomics detects and subtypes esophageal cancer
summary: In 1260 participants, machine learning models on plasma circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA fragmentomic profiles detected esophageal cancer with AUC 0.9706 in training and 0.9762 internal, 0.9748 external and 0.9668 minority-population validation. Sensitivity for stage I cancer was 92.16% in the combined validation cohort, and the model identified 93.10% of early cancers missed by preoperative biopsy. A second model separated squamous cell carcinoma from adenocarcinoma with 89.71% accuracy.
ai_technology: Machine learning models on plasma cell-free mtDNA fragmentomic profiles (detection and subtyping)
organization: Tang Du Hospital; Air Force Medical University

evidence.tested: Training plus internal, external and Chinese minority (Uyghur and Kazakh) validation cohorts (1260 participants).
evidence.unknown: Retrospective multicenter design; prospective screening performance and the specific algorithms are not stated in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning classifies cancer status and histological subtype from fragmentomic features.
